subject: Dual-fabric tenant egress policy review — walkthrough and asks
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@cumuluscloud.com>
Cc: Cumulus Infra <infra@cumuluscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dual-fabric tenant egress policy review — walkthrough and asks

Hi all,

Thanks for agreeing to review the dual-fabric topology draft (attached). This thread is to collect feedback on tenant egress controls for the private VPC deployment we discussed in the kickoff. Key goals for this review:

- Validate where tenant NAT/eBPF enforcement should live (edge vs. tenant-side).
- Confirm failover semantics between Fabric-A (control/data shared plane) and Fabric-B (data-only fast path).
- Agree on latency SLAs for short-path vs. long-path fallbacks and acceptable percentiles.
- Identify any compliance artifacts we need to produce (egress audit logs, prefix allowlist proof).

Attachments: dual-fabric-draft-v1.png (diagram), egress-policy-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix of tenant policies we've started).

Specific asks: please comment inline in the Drive diagram or reply here with:
1) Any operational blockers (BGP, cross-connect constraints) you foresee for colocated customers.
2) Minimum telemetry points we need to collect to prove egress isolation (sample points + retention).
3) If we should centralize KMS for egress key wrapping or let tenants manage their own keys behind the private control plane.

Alex — would you and the Cumulus infra team call out any expected crossconnect/BGP constraints from your side?

Proposed meeting if we need to sync: Thu 2027-07-08 10:00 PT (30m). If that works for everyone I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@cumuluscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dual-fabric tenant egress policy review — walkthrough and asks

Thanks Mateo — quick feedback after scanning the diagram and matrix:

- NAT placement: prefer tenant-side egress NAT on Fabric-B (fast path) for performance, but require a central NAT gateway on Fabric-A for fallback and inventory tracking.
- Failover semantics: we should define an active/active health check that fails over to Fabric-A within 250ms for control-plane heartbeats and 500ms for long-lived flows (document in runbook).
- Telemetry: at minimum collect (1) per-tenant egress byte counters (1m rollup), (2) per-tenant outbound flow logs (sample 1:1000), (3) per-attachment BGP state. Retention: 90 days for counters, 365 days for flow sampling for security incidents.
- KMS: central KMS for egress wrapping is OK if we can produce key usage audit logs per-tenant. If customers demand tenant-managed keys, mark as "allowed but unsupported" for initial GA.

I left inline comments on the Drive diagram on the proposed NAT breakout and control-plane route leaking concerns. Also added a column in the matrix for required audit evidence (see egress-policy-matrix-v2.xlsx).

No strong objections from my side to the proposed meeting time.

— Kim
Kimberly Park
Lead Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: egress-policy-matrix-v2.xlsx]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cumuluscloud.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dual-fabric tenant egress policy review — walkthrough and asks

Appreciate the rundown, Mateo. A couple of items from the Cumulus infra side:

- Crossconnects: our colo partners typically allow two L2 circuits per tenant for redundancy, but on some sites the second circuit is billed as a premium. We can provision single-circuit with LACP; we should call that out as a risk for our multi-path assumptions.
- BGP: if you plan to accept customer ASN peering we need to confirm AS path prep and AS-PATH filtering. We can provide a template ACL and we expect the customer to advertise only verified prefixes.
- Egress NAT hairpinning: Avoid hairpin NAT across fabrics — we’ve seen asymmetric routing cause session breakage. Recommend keep return path symmetric by tagging flows with path identifiers and enforcing return in the same fabric.

Questions:
1) For tenants that demand tenant-managed KMS, will the control plane be able to validate key rotation status (we need an API contract)?
2) Do you have an initial performance target for Fabric-B latency (p50/p95)?

We can attend Thu 10:00 PT. I’ll bring the crossconnect SLA doc and a short checklist for peering prep.

— Alex Turner
Principal Infra Engineer, Cumulus Cloud Solutions
Cumulus Cloud Solutions

Subject: Re: Dual-fabric tenant egress policy review — walkthrough and asks

Thanks everyone — summary and agreed next steps below so we have a single source of truth before the call: 

Agreed outcomes prior to GA:
- NAT strategy: tenant-side NAT on Fabric-B; central NAT gateway on Fabric-A for fallback and billing/audit.
- Failover: active/active health checks; failover window target: control-plane 250ms, long-flow fallback 500ms.
- Telemetry: collect per-tenant counters (1m), sampled flow logs (1:1000), BGP attach events; retention 90d/365d as Kim suggested.
- KMS: GA uses central KMS with tenant usage audit logs. Tenant-managed keys allowed as opt-in for later release; define API contract for rotation validation (action: SOON-Assign to API team).
- Crossconnects/BGP: Alex to provide crossconnect SLA doc and peering ACL template prior to cutover. Note single-circuit sites are a risk — catalogue in site readiness doc.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Alex: send crossconnect SLA + peering checklist (By: Mon 2027-07-12).
- Kim: finalize runbook snippets for failover thresholds and telemetry collection points; add to RED-4521 (By: Wed 2027-07-14).
- Mateo: schedule Thu 10:00 PT meeting and add Drive links; update diagram with Kim's inline comments (By: Thu 2027-07-08).
- Soojin: draft the KMS API contract stub and circulate with Security (By: Fri 2027-07-16).

Meeting scheduled: Thu 2027-07-08 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-dual-fabric

If anyone disagrees with the summary, reply-all and we’ll adjust before the meeting.

— Soojin
